record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Develop a theory of non-coercive integral input-to-state Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems, including their basic properties and their usefulness for proving iISS. At present this non-coercive iISS Lyapunov theory has not been investigated.

evidence.quote: • Properties of non-coercive iISS Lyapunov functions have not been investigated right now.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an abstract control system $\Sigma = (X, \mathcal{U}, \phi)$ where $(X, \|\cdot\|_X)$ is a Banach space (the state space), $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed vector space of admissible input functions $u : \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \to U$ with values in a normed space $U$, and $\phi : D_\phi \subset \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \times X \times \mathcal{U} \to X$ is a transition map satisfying the usual axioms (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity).

Recall the standard comparison-function classes: $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\mathcal{L}$, and $\mathcal{KL}$.

The system $\Sigma$ is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\alpha, \gamma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for all $x \in X$, all admissible $u \in \mathcal{U}$, and all $t \geq 0$,
$$\alpha(\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X) \leq \beta(\|x\|_X, t) + \int_0^t \gamma(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds.$$

A continuous function $V : X \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $V(0)=0$ is called a coercive iISS Lyapunov function if there exist $\psi_1, \psi_2 \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ (or positive definite), and $\sigma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
$$\psi_1(\|x\|_X) \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X), \qquad \dot V_u(x) \leq -\alpha(\|x\|_X) + \sigma(\|u\|_U),$$
where $\dot V_u$ denotes an appropriate (Dini or Lie) derivative of $V$ along trajectories. Dropping the lower bound $\psi_1(\|x\|_X) \leq V(x)$ (so only $0 \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X)$ is required) yields a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function candidate.

Develop a theory of non-coercive integral input-to-state Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems of the above type. Specifically:

(a) Identify the appropriate definition (or definitions) of a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function for $\Sigma$.

(b) Establish their basic properties (existence, regularity, behaviour along trajectories, relations to coercive iISS Lyapunov functions, and converse-Lyapunov style results).

(c) Prove sufficient conditions under which the existence of a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function implies that $\Sigma$ is iISS, and identify minimal additional regularity hypotheses (e.g., on the semigroup, well-posedness, or admissibility of the input operator) needed for such an implication.
artifact.status_search_result: Non-coercive Lyapunov function theory for infinite-dimensional systems has been substantially developed since 2019 (Mironchenko–Wirth, JDE 2019; SIAM J. Control Optim. 2020), extending to ISS and to certain iISS/LISS settings via norm-to-integral ISS characterizations and constructions for time-varying semilinear evolution equations. However, a fully developed theory of non-coercive iISS Lyapunov functions with general converse results matching the coercive case does not yet appear in the literature; recent works (e.g., 2025 papers on coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular systems and 2025 time-varying evolution equation results) treat related but partial settings. The problem is therefore best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Non-coercive Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Non-coercive Lyapunov functions are sufficient for UGAS of infinite-dimensional systems with external disturbances under mild assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results on non-coercive Lyapunov functions exist for infinite-dimensional systems with disturbances.

status_evidence.title: Noncoercive Lyapunov Functions for Input-to-State Stability of Infinite-Dimensional Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Noncoercive Lyapunov functions imply norm-to-integral ISS, equivalent to ISS under regularity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Non-coercive ISS Lyapunov theory has been developed, partially covering integral aspects.

status_evidence.title: Lyapunov methods for input-to-state stability of time-varying evolution equations
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of non-coercive LISS/iISS Lyapunov functions for time-varying semi-linear evolution equations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constructions of non-coercive iISS Lyapunov functions exist for restricted classes.

status_evidence.title: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems (2025).
status_evidence.claim: Recent companion work focuses on coercive case, indicating non-coercive iISS theory remains less complete.
